thread.text:
Most web driving games use an arcade "press Space to drift" hack.

We built an endless EV drifter driven by actual weight-transfer physics: brake to load the front axle, pin the throttle to break the rear loose, countersteer to catch the slide.

No handbrake button. All in 1 HTML file. 🧵👇
thread.mediaNote: GIF of a sleek EV initiating a clean pendulum drift around a snow bend into a zombie horde, switching between cockpit HUD and top-down view.

thread.text:
The tire model runs on pure Newtonian slip curves:

• Braking transfers vehicle mass forward, unloading the rear
• Instant electric torque overwhelms the unweighted rear tires
• Countersteering balances slip angle against momentum

Cut the throttle mid-slide and dynamic regen kicks in to snap the car straight while recharging your pack.
thread.mediaNote: Short video showing dynamic suspension telemetry and tire friction vectors overlaying the car during an entry slide.

thread.text:
Zero audio samples were used.

The EV motor whine is synthesized in real time via procedural WebAudio:
• Pitch modulates with instantaneous wheel RPM
• Loudness scales with kW power draw
• Harmonics invert with a downward sweep under regenerative braking

Deterministic daily seeds let you race against exact ghost telemetry lines.
thread.mediaNote: Audio clip demonstration isolating the WebAudio procedural motor synth across acceleration, coasting, and hard regen.

thread.text:
The entire stack—Canvas rendering, tire physics, procedural biomes, weapon systems, and audio engine—lives in a single, zero-dependency HTML file.

No npm install. No 50MB asset packs. Instant 0.1s load time on mobile and desktop.

The open web can still feel lightweight and instantaneous.
